name: Carrot

companions.note: Borage attracts predatory insects that control carrot fly
Tomatoes repel carrot fly; carrots may loosen soil around tomato roots

antagonists.note: Alliums can stunt carrot growth when planted in close proximity

pnw_notes: Carrots left in the ground through Portland winters sweeten as starches convert to sugar in the cold — this is one of the best uses of a fall bed. Sow in late summer (July–August) for fall harvest, or leave summer-sown carrots in the ground and harvest through winter as needed. Needs deep, loose, rock-free soil — raised beds are ideal. Thin ruthlessly to 3 in or roots fork.

planting_windows.notes: Sow for fall/winter harvest; keep soil consistently moist until germination (10–21 days)
Harvest as needed through winter; sweetness peaks after sustained cold. Mulch tops to protect from hard freezes.
